title: Cover a bowl of rising dough with a cloth: take a washcloth off a towel stand with both hands and lay it over the rim
instruction: Cover the bowl of dough with the cloth so it can rise.
context: A small batch of bread dough (about two rolls' worth) is covered with a clean cloth while it rises so its surface does not dry into a skin. The cloth is the one hanging on the countertop towel stand just behind the bowl. The robot takes the two bottom corners of the side facing it, one hand from each side, draws the cloth toward itself so it slides over the bar and comes off, lays it over the bowl and lets go. The cloth is limp: a free-hanging side swings away from the first pad that touches it, and once off the bar the cloth follows the hands. Laid short it leaves the far rim bare; pulled too far it slides back off the far side or drags the light glass bowl; lowered onto the bowl it presses on the dough. It must end covering the whole rim with at least 2 cm hanging past it all round, clear of the dough, off the stand, with the bowl and the stand where they were.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the counter. 1) Towel stand: Gatco 1444SN countertop hand-towel holder, satin-nickel steel, T-shaped, 267 wide (y) x 283 high, on a weighted padded rectangular base 89 deep (x); 0.73 kg. Base 140 wide and 15 thick, post 12 and bar 13 across (estimates). Bar along y, its axis at x = 285, y centred on 0. 2) Bowl: Duralex Lys 14 cm, clear tempered glass, 140 across the rim, 55 high, 500 ml; foot 70 across, wall 4.5, bottom 6 (estimates that give the 500 ml); about 270 g (estimate). Foot centred at (150, 0), so its far rim is 20 in front of the stand's base. 3) Dough stand-in: one 4 oz (112 g) can of white Play-Doh pressed into the bottom as a centred dome 80 across and 26 high, its top 23 below the rim (shape it by ruler). 4) Cloth: one Burt's Bees Baby organic cotton woven terry washcloth, Blue Solid, 254 x 254 (10 x 10 in), about 29 g and 2.5 thick (estimates). It hangs over the bar, hems parallel to it, centred on y = 0: 165 of cloth from the bar's top down the side facing the robot (that hem 125 above the counter), 89 down the back (hem 200 up). Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open. Frictions are estimates (cloth 1.5 in the simulator, stand 0.30, glass 0.45).
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from the top-camera video, a top photo, a side photo through the clear bowl with a ruler stood behind it, and a flexible tape. A part of the rim is covered when, in the top photo, the cloth hides it. Overhang: along the cloth from the rim's outer edge to the nearest cloth edge, where it is shortest. Score 0 if either gripper still holds the cloth or is within 2 cm of it, the cloth is still moving (any point more than 1 cm from where it was 1 s earlier), no part of the rim is covered (doing nothing scores 0), the bowl tipped more than 15 degrees at any time, the bowl's centre moved more than 2 cm, or the towel stand was knocked over or moved more than 2 cm (in simulation the stand is fixed). Otherwise the lowest of: (1) rim covered: 1.0 if all of it; 0.5 if at least 75 % but not all; 0.25 if under 75 %. (2) shortest overhang: 1.0 if at least 2 cm; 0.75 if at least 1 cm and under 2 cm; 0.5 if under 1 cm. (3) bowl moved: 1.0 if at most 1 cm; 0.75 if more than 1 cm. (4) dough: 1.0 if the cloth does not touch the dough and its lowest point inside the rim is at most 1.5 cm below the rim's top; 0.75 if it does not touch but hangs lower; 0.5 if it touches. (5) stand: 1.0 if no part of the cloth is left on the stand's bar; 0.25 if some is. Simulation checks the rim every 5 degrees; touching = a cloth node within 2.75 mm of the dome.
reset_notes: About 2 minutes. Lift the cloth off by hand. Stand the bowl back with its foot centred at (150, 0) on its pencil circle and the towel stand's base on its tape outline; if the cloth touched the dough, re-shape the Play-Doh dome by ruler (80 across, 26 high, top 23 below the rim). Keep the Play-Doh in its can between sessions and use a fresh can after 10 trials or when it cracks or dries. Shake the cloth out and hang it over the bar, hems parallel to the bar and centred on it, smooth face toward the robot, with its front hem 125 above the counter and the back hem 200 up (ruler), no folds; let it stop swinging. Use a fresh cloth from the pack when it is creased, damp or marked, and after 20 trials; wash and dry used ones before reuse. Both arms to the ready pose, grippers open.
fidelity: The cloth is true PhysX cloth (1,369 nodes), spawned hanging over the bar; its bend stiffness makes a 30 mm lip droop about 8 mm, as estimated for the real cloth. While both pads press the cloth it is pinned to the gripper (PhysX cloth has no static friction); opening releases it, and nothing else does. The towel stand is fixed; the dough is a rigid dome in the bowl. A let-go hem may tremble a few mm, so stillness is judged over 1 s. Masses, thicknesses, droop and frictions are estimates.
